attributes.body_ja:
「しかも」は「さらに」や「その上（うえ）」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）す接続詞（せつぞくし）です。(A) と (B) が同時（どうじ）に成（な）り立（た）っていること、または並行（へいこう）して存在（そんざい）していることを表（あらわ）します。「しかも」は話題（わだい）全体（ぜんたい）に焦点（しょうてん）を当（あ）てて使（つか）われ、主観的（しゅかんてき）な意見（いけん）よりも客観的（きゃっかんてき）な意見（いけん）（目（め）で見（み）てわかる事実（じじつ））を述（の）べるときに使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。

「しかも」は接続詞（せつぞくし）なので、二（ふた）つの文（ぶん）の間（あいだ）に置（お）かれたり、前（まえ）の文（ぶん）を受（う）けて、次（つぎ）の文（ぶん）や節（せつ）の頭（あたま）で使（つか）われたりします。

多（おお）くの場合（ばあい）、(A) は基本的（きほんてき）な情報（じょうほう）とされ、(B) はその上（うえ）に加（くわ）えられる追加（ついか）情報（じょうほう）や補足（ほそく）説明（せつめい）になります。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「しかも」は古語（こご）の間投詞（かんとうし）「然（しか）」（意味（いみ）：そう）と助詞（じょし）「も」を組（く）み合（あ）わせたものです。この「しか」は前（まえ）に述（の）べられた内容（ないよう）を「そうだ」と認（みと）めるもので、これに「も」が付（つ）くことで、「(A) を認（みと）めつつ、その上（うえ）に (B) を加（くわ）える」という「しかも」という言葉（ことば）になっています。

豆知識（まめちしき）

現代（げんだい）では、書（か）き言葉（ことば）として「而（しか）も」や「併（しか）も」という表記（ひょうき）が見（み）れらることもありますが、どちらも非常（ひじょう）に稀（まれ）な表現（ひょうげん）です。
attributes.body:
しかも is a conjunction in Japanese which is commonly translated as either 'furthermore', or 'moreover'. This is a somewhat formal grammar pattern which indicates that both (A) and (B) exist at the same time, or are in unison. しかも itself focuses on the overall topic, so will be used for giving objective opinions, such as observable facts, rather than personal opinions.

As しかも is a conjunction, it may be used between two phrases, or sometimes at the beginning of a second sentence, when referring back to the first.

Often, (A) will be considered the 'base' information, while (B) is extra information added on top of (A), or further explaining (A).

Fun-fact

Originally, しかも came from the combination of the archaic interjection 然（しか） 'as such', or 'like that', and the particle も 'too', or 'also'. In this way, some reflection can be seen between it and modern English phrases like 'additionally', where the (B) information is simply adding on to what is already known about (A).

Fun-fact

In modern writing, しかも may also appear as either 而（しか）も or 併（しか）も, although both are quite rare.

それに and しかも both add information, but しかも is stronger. それに is neutral: it adds a point that logically follows. しかも emphasizes what comes next, like 'what's more' or 'on top of that', e.g. 安い。それに美味しい。しかも体にいい ('It's cheap. And tasty. And what's more, it's good for your body.').

その上 and しかも can both appear at the beginning of a sentence to introduce additional information. They are often interchangeable, but しかも is somewhat more colloquial and can imply that the added information is unexpected. その上 is more neutral and formal, with no such implication.

Both add extra information. しかも is neutral, adding notable facts, as in 彼は優秀だ。しかも親切だ (He’s talented, and moreover, kind). おまけに can add positive or negative on top of that nuance, as in 雨だった。おまけに風も強かった (It was raining, and on top of that, the wind was strong).

second_relatable.title: おまけに
second_relatable.meaning: In addition, On top of that, What is more, To make matters worse

attributes.body: Both add information, but differ in nuance. しかも emphasizes reinforcement or surprising addition, as in この料理はおいしい。しかも安い (This dish is delicious. And what’s more, it’s cheap). 更に is more formal, indicating progression or escalation, as in 明日は更に寒くなるでしょう (Tomorrow it will get even colder).

second_relatable.title: 更に
second_relatable.meaning: Even more or further, Again, More and more

attributes.body: Both express addition like the English 'moreover', but differ in usage. しかも starts a sentence to add information that emphasizes the previous point, e.g. '彼は優秀だ。しかも努力家だ' ('He's talented. Moreover, he's hardworking'). 又〜も, because of も, must be used with another noun that also applies and adds to the previous statement, e.g. '姉はピアノが弾ける。また、歌も歌える' ('My older sister can play piano. She can also sing songs').

second_relatable.title: 又〜も
second_relatable.meaning: Moreover, Additionally, And also, In addition, Furthermore, Or

attributes.body: しかも and なお② both add additional information, but differ in nuance. しかも often strengthens the previous statement with surprising or emphatic detail, as in 彼は優秀だ。しかも努力家だ (He is talented, and what’s more, hardworking). なお② is more neutral and formal, used to supply further facts without emphasis, as in 今回の件について、なお調査中です (Regarding this matter, we are still investigating further).
